summary_out.changed: Dropped the L1 5s position-age override. Replaced it with an adverse-move signal-strength override: when the cap is hit by a REVERSAL order (opposite side of current position), admit it only if the mid-price has moved adversely against the entry by >= 1 MES tick ($0.25) since the position opened. Same-direction adds at/above cap remain skipped (matching base). Reduce-only orders always submit.
summary_out.outcome: pnl +4737.57% vs simple baseline ($2092.25 vs $43.25 over 11 apples-to-apples dates), sharpe 10.08, slippage 0.0/0.0. Gate vs simple: PASS. BUT vs base_algo position-tier-gate on the same 11 dates ($3564.25 / 73,802 trades): -41.30% pnl, +9.80% trade_count. All 11 per-date pnls underperform base; 3 dates (20260313, 20260316, 20260317) flipped from positive to negative under l2. Hypothesis PARTIALLY VINDICATED (signal-strength direction is right -- L1 was -75.3%, L2 is -41.3%, a +34 pp recovery on one change) but the threshold of 1 tick is too low: 7,232 extra admitted reversals are net money-losing because 1 tick of adverse mid-move is bid-ask oscillation, not a regime change. Sharpe 10.08 over 11 days is a small-N artifact -- treat as directional only; realized_pnl is the bottom line and on that L2 is materially worse than base.
summary_out.hypothesis: L1 next text said the highest-leverage axis was signal-strength rather than time. The executor cannot read the oracle's edge magnitude, but the cleanest microstructure proxy is the adverse-move on the underlying since the existing position was opened: if the market has moved against the current position by >= 1 tick, the original entry is empirically losing and reversing it is rational; if the market has not moved adversely, the flip is far more likely to be noise oscillation that the base correctly skips. The same gate skeleton was preserved; only the override predicate changed from age-based to adverse-move-based. I explicitly bet against the 1-tick threshold being too low and lost that bet -- the predicate is right but the level is wrong.
summary_out.brief_summary: ptg-b-l2 (position-tier-gate brief-summary loop 2) dropped L1's age override and replaced it with an adverse-move predicate: admit cap-hit reversal OPENs only when mid has moved >= 1 tick against the existing position. Result: PASS vs simple (+4737.57% pnl) and a substantial recovery from L1 (-75.3% -> -41.3% vs base), but still materially WORSE than base on the same 11 dates. All 11 per-date pnls trail base; 3 marginal days flip from positive to negative. Mechanism: the signal-strength axis is correct (one-tick predicate beats the age predicate by +34 pp), but the threshold is too permissive -- 7,232 extra admitted reversals are net money-losing because 1 tick of adverse move is bid-ask oscillation, not real regime change. Sharpe 10.08 over 11 days is small-N inflated; realized_pnl is the bottom line. The same prediction the hypothesis explicitly bet against (1 tick too low) is what played out.
summary_out.next: Raise adverse_threshold_ticks from 1 to 3 ($0.75 in price, 3 full-spread displacements against the original entry). The L2 hypothesis section identified the exact two failure modes -- too low admits noise, too high collapses to base -- and L2 landed at the noisy end. 3 ticks is the natural single-step probe: it requires a meaningful adverse regime ('original entry was wrong by 3 ticks of mid-move'), not bid-ask oscillation. Key in-flight diagnostic: if L3 still has +trade_count vs base, the predicate is still admitting too many reversals and L4 should test 5 ticks. If L3 collapses to ~0 admitted reversals (trade_count ~= base), L4 should probe 2 ticks. If L3 underperforms base even at 3 ticks, the adverse-mid axis is exhausted as a proxy and L4 should pivot to a different conditioning variable (spread vs rolling median, signed aggressor imbalance). Avoid: any return to age-only filters; any threshold < 1 tick.
